title: Prevent cross-tenant admission bypass that causes intermittent long-context tail spikes
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Summary: Several customers on Hosted and Dedicated reported intermittent tail-latency spikes when the system was handling mixed short and long-context traffic. Root cause analysis shows a rare admission accounting bypass in the hybrid batching path that allowed some requests to bypass admission reservoirs during KV-cache churn, resulting in microbursts that starved latency-sensitive tenants and produced long-context tail spikes. This ticket scopes the bugfix, validation, rollout, and postmortem actions across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy runtime-1.22 with hybrid-batcher enabled and KV cache eviction threshold at default

2) Generate mixed workload: 70% short (<=64 tokens) high-qps from tenant A and 30% long (>=2048 tokens) from tenant B, interleaved with sustained KV churn (simulate model reloads or tokenize variability)
3) Observe admission reservoir metrics: some short requests are recorded as admitted but not reflected in reservoir accounting during a prefetch/eviction window
4) Notice small-request queue sizes drop then backlog of long-context batches grows causing tail latency spikes for both tenants
5) Reproduce intermittently with seed traffic patterns and high KV eviction rate (use synthetic workload harness in perf-lab)
root_cause: A race in the hybrid batcher admission path: when a request hits an in-flight KV-cache eviction/prefetch handshake, the fast-path bypassed the admission decrement in a rare ordering. The request was allowed to proceed (short path) but the admission reservoir did not record the dequeue, so the effective admitted count drifted positive. Under mixed load that drift accumulates and the scheduler over-admits short flows, starving the slot budget for long-context batches and amplifying tail latency.
proposed_fix: Add an atomic admission token lifecycle that couples admit/dequeue with the KV prefetch handshake (always update the reservoir under the same lock or via an atomic CAS)
Instrument and assert admission invariants in debug builds (admitted_count == enqueued_count - dequeued_count) and fail fast in canary to catch regressions
Introduce a temporary admission back-pressure gate that rejects/queues bypassed fast-paths when reservoir drift is detected (>2% drift over 30s)
Add targeted unit and e2e tests that simulate KV eviction interleavings and tenant mixes to prevent regressions
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR to feature branch with instrumentation and safety gate
2) Run perf-lab fuzz harness for 48h against synthetic mixed workloads
3) Canary deploy to Hosted region us-west with runtime-1.22-canary for 6 hours, monitor admission invariants and tail percentiles
4) If stable, expand canary to Dedicated pools with customer-simulated traffic (Acme Payments test cluster)
5) Schedule Private on-prem customers upgrades with opt-in patch and provide clear rollback steps
6) Full rollout across Hosted after 72h stable canary and sign-off from SRE and Product
monitoring_and_telemetry: Add alert: admission_drift_high (>2% sustained over 30s) -> P0 page to SRE
Trace sampling for requests that hit the fast-path during KV eviction windows (attach trace id to admission token lifecycle)
Dashboard: tenant-level admitted_vs_enqueued vs tail_p99.9 over time
customer_reports: INC-2026-1126: Acme Payments - recurring p95/p99 latency spikes during business hours (hosted)
INC-2026-1173: HealthCo - Dedicated pool showed degraded throughput and customer reported model timeouts
